messages:
Maria S.: Hey team — inbound from AcmeCorp: they're getting 429s around 11:23 UTC but Console shows ~75% quota remaining for their token. Customer sent request_id=req_0a9f and a screenshot. Any immediate thoughts?

Alex P.: Can you paste the request id + exact timestamp? Also which deployment (hosted/dedicated)?

Maria S.: req_0a9f, ts=2026-03-10T11:23:12Z, hosted-us-west, plan=standard. Screenshot shows Console available=15k tokens at 11:23. Customer says they were blocked.

Sriram K.: Looking at enforcer logs: enforcement returned 429 for req=req_0a9f at 11:23:12. Emitted usage event to kafka topic 'enforcer-usage'. Pulling analytics consumer traces now.

Alex P.: Is this the snapshot/aggregation lag we've seen before? @Sriram any trace ids?

Sriram K.: Found it — enforcer emitted event (offset 345678). Analytics consumer acked but snapshotter commit lagged ~92s due to a GC pause on the node running the consumer. Query against analytics store shows zero tokens at that time. Example SQL: 
SELECT sum(tokens) FROM quota_events WHERE token_id='tok_acme123' AND time < '2026-03-10T11:23:30Z'; -- returns 0

Maria S.: Customer timeline: 11:23:12 -> 11:24:00 got 429s; console UI reflected the consumption around 11:25. They want an explanation and rollback if enforcement was wrong.

Alex P.: Short-term message: enforcement is source of truth; console lagged because snapshotter/aggregator was slow. Proposed customer messaging: 'Quota was consumed; analytics snapshot lag caused stale numbers in the UI. Enforcement acted correctly.' Thoughts?

Kevin L.: Mitigation idea: start copying enforcer events to realtime-metrics (different sink) so Console can show a "realtime" indicator from that feed. Can enable for affected customers while we fix snapshotter.

Maria S.: :thumbsup: I'll notify the account with that wording. Can we also provide repro steps for SRE?

Sriram K.: Repro steps: 1) Generate a short burst of concurrent requests with the affected token. 2) Tail /var/log/enforcer/enforcer.log and confirm 429s. 3) Curl the console snapshot endpoint and observe ~60-90s lag. Commands: 
```bash
hey -n 200 -c 50 -m POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok_acme123' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -D payload.json
tail -f /var/log/enforcer/enforcer.log | grep req_0a9f
curl -s 'https://console.redwood.ai/api/console/quota-snapshot?token=tok_acme123'
```

Alex P.: Root cause hypothesis: snapshotter uses microbatch commit window set to 1m; the GC pause caused consumer to miss heartbeat and commit was delayed. Plan: reduce batch window to 20s + run a backfill to reindex the last 5m for affected tokens. I'll open a PR and propose a staging deploy.

Sriram K.: Created ticket INF-1298 and added runbook: 1) restart analytics-consumer if lag > 30s, 2) trigger backfill for token range, 3) enable temporary copy to realtime sink. Also adding an alert for console-snapshot-lag > 30s when consumption delta > 10%.

Maria S.: I've messaged the customer with an interim explanation and timeline. They accepted the update and asked for follow-up once we have a permanent fix.

deploy-bot: analytics-consumer v1.14.2 deployed to staging (sha:abc123) :rocket:

Kevin L.: Quick win: add "last-updated" timestamp and a small warning on the Console quota panel when snapshot age > 30s. Low-risk UX change.

Maria S.: Good call. I'll track CIF and follow up once PRs merge. Thanks all.
